industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, because the industry is split and the sector rows carry the view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Chris Wood (via Jefferies, 17 Oct) would diversify from artificial intelligence into healthcare and financials, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, C prior at industry level, with Medtech capital goods at A; but pharmaceuticals against medical technology was not spoken to by any source, clinical-stage biotech is the unproven, cash-burning end the Fragility axis punishes (B.11 at D, relative strength F), and only five of the 149 Pool stocks are healthcare. Pharma/biotech and Hospitals carry B. Counter-case for B at the industry: 94 stocks, the second largest industry, and a defensive rotation that is now five weeks old; for D: a crowded destination.

sector.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Wood (via Jefferies, 17 Oct) names healthcare as the diversification from artificial intelligence, Healthcare's industry relative strength rose to B, and large pharma is the large, proven, cash-yielding case the regime pays for; pharmaceuticals against medical technology was not spoken to, so the row rests on the regime and the rotation, not on a pharma call. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: C now, D prior. One Pool name (Genmab, Sell-side A, TSR/Valuation A on the valuation reading only). Counter-case: a defensive destination five weeks into a rotation is crowded, and the franc and dollar move the Swiss and UK names' reported earnings.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried unchanged on this week's reading. Goldman Sachs (16 Oct) has French spreads at decade highs with tentative spillover to Italy and judges France's fiscal challenge 'harder now than in 2011-15'; the premium in basis points was not read, so the reversal conditions (back to D under 120 basis points, to C under 100) could not be tested and are plainly not met at a decade high. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Relative strength is not graded by country; no live holding is French-listed. Counter-case unchanged: a country letter is a blunt tool on 110 stocks and lands on French-listed global businesses (TotalEnergies, whose memo exposures lift its Thematic Fit/Momentum by two grades through the stock layer; Soitec; Sopra Steria; Alten) as hard as on domestic banks and property; and Goldman's own judgement is that disorderly escalation is less likely than in 2011-15.
